messages:
maria: Quick one — auditor wants 'snapshot scenarios' for SOC2 evidence handoff. They specifically called out RBAC changes, KMS rotation proof, vuln triage timeline, and linking those to incident records. What minimal artifacts do we hand them?
kevin: TL;DR: per scenario we should provide 1) control mapping spreadsheet row, 2) signed manifest + checksums, 3) time-bounded logs (rbac/k8s/iam) covering the window, 4) KMS rotation record + CMK policy snapshot, 5) vuln ticket with triage notes and patch timeline, 6) incident ID cross-ref if applicable. Keep it small. :white_check_mark:
danny: +1. Also include the automation commands we used to generate snapshots (so auditors can reproduce). e.g.
```
# export RBAC bindings for time window
./tools/audit-export --type=rbackind --from=2023-09-15T00:00:00Z --to=2023-09-16T00:00:00Z --out=rbac-20230915.json
# collect KMS key rotation history
aws kms list-keys --profile prod | jq '.' > keys.json
aws kms get-key-rotation-status --key-id <key> --output json > rotation-status.json
```
kevin: Good point, include the SHA256 checksums of exported files and a simple chain-of-custody file: who ran export, host, hash, upload time, S3 path. auditors often ask for reproducibility.\nauditor_jane: For the KMS items we need the rotation event time, the CMK policy version used, and proof that the old key material is not reused. Also want a statement of who had Decrypt or ScheduleKeyDeletion privileges at the time. Is that in the IAM logs?
sophia: We can extract that from the authz events. Recommendation: provide an "access-snapshot.csv" showing users/roles with dangerous privileges at the snapshot time. Use the last committed policy and attach the policy diff.
sec-sre-bot: evidence-collector v2.3 completed export: rbac-20230915.json (sha256: e3b0c442...), rotation-status.json (sha256: a7c1f2...), vuln-triage-3721.json (sha256: 9f2c3d...) — uploaded to s3://redwood-audit/2023-09-15-evidence/ (presigned links expire in 7d).
kevin: Auditor will also ask about sampling rationale. For older controls we should include a short note: why we picked X window (e.g., change occurred on Y date; sampling window +/- 24h covers rollout/rollback). Put that in control-mapping.csv under a "sampling_reason" column.
danny: On vuln triage: attach the ticket (JIRA/linear URL), triage notes (who validated, CVSS, PoC?), remediation plan, deploy PRs, and the patch rollout timeline (canary -> full). Auditors want evidence of closure and verification.
auditor_jane: Also need to see that incident 2023-09-15 (if referenced) has preserved forensic snapshots — screenshots of the alert, raw logs used in triage, and the postmortem link. Redact PII if present.
sophia: I'll prepare two artifacts: (1) a zipped evidence bundle with manifest + checksums + chain-of-custody.txt, (2) control crosswalk spreadsheet mapping each piece to SOC2/ISO control IDs. I can redact dev emails and replace with role placeholders.
maria: Perfect. Can you include a short runbook snippet explaining how to re-generate the RBAC snapshot? Auditors sometimes ask for procedural steps. Keep it 4-6 lines.
sophia: Yup. Example snippet will go in README.txt inside the bundle.
kevin: Ops question — where do we store the final signed evidence? We prefer an artifacts bucket with MFA-delete and limited retention. Proposed path: s3://redwood-audit/closed-audits/<audit-id>/evidence-<date>.zip (access via presigned URL, 7 days, then rotate).
danny: We should also log who downloaded the presigned link. Add a small access manifest entry: presign-user, ip, timestamp.
auditor_jane: One more: for RBAC changes, auditors might want to see approval trail for the change (PR approvals, JIRA signoff). If available, include the PR diff and approval evidence.
sophia: I'll pull PR metadata (author, reviewers, merge time) and include a screenshot of approvals.
kevin: If any evidence contains secrets, redact and replace with placeholder and reference the original safe copy in HSM-backed archive — include an attestation that the redaction was performed and by whom.
maria: Sounds like a plan. Thanks — can we aim to have a draft bundle by EOD tomorrow? :hourglass_flowing_sand:
sophia: I'll start the export now and post the draft presigned links here when ready.
sec-sre-bot: evidence-collector started job 7891 (expected runtime ~12m)
kevin: Thanks team, keep the messages concise in the bundle. Auditors prefer short evidence descriptions; store longer notes in the internal control-mapping doc only.
maria: Great. Closing — will follow up if auditor asks for deeper chain-of-custody. :thumbsup:
